cs.t: A year of plugging it in once or twice a day to recharge it, and it blew. Old rectangular USB-A was only rated for 1500 ideal insertions.  USB-C is a big improvement at 10,000 ideal insertions.  Most insertions are not ideal, and it is relatively common to have some leveraged pressure trying to wedge the port apart; When my phone bridges the gap between the arm of the sofa and the coffee table while plugged in, for example, it's got a bending moment.  USB-C is much thinner in the up-down dimension than USB-A, and it is not designed to safely disengage when side-loaded like Magsafe.  If you  wanted  to break it for some reason, I'm pretty sure you could do it in a few seconds while resting your elbows on the table, on grip strength alone.

cs.t: Thanks god the headphone jacks died in smartphones. I switched to USB-C soundcard cables which are dirt cheap and survive much much more plug-unplug-cycles. They easily can be replaced.

cs.t: The USB-C charging ports on my phones have always collected lint to the point they totally stop working and have to be cleaned out vigorously. I don't know how this problem is so much worse with USB-C or the physics behind it, but it's a very common issue. This port could be improved for sure.
